MK-6482-004 (Phase 2, open-label study of belzutifan in patients with VHL disease-associated non-metastatic RCC) formed the basis for evaluation of the efficacy of belzutifan in the indicated population.

design.text: Ongoing single-arm, open-label, international Phase 2 study; belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily.

citations.quote: Study MK-6482-004 is an ongoing single-arm open-label Phase 2 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of belzutifan in participants with VHL disease and at least 1 measurable RCC tumor (as defined by RECIST 1.1). Participants received belzutifan 120 mg by oral administration once daily.

population.text: Patients with VHL disease-associated RCC with at least 1 measurable solid RCC tumor and no RCC tumor >3.0 cm requiring immediate surgery; excluded prior systemic anticancer therapy and metastatic disease.

citations.quote: Enrollment criteria for MK-6482-004 included at least 1 measurable solid RCC tumor and no RCC tumor >3.0 cm that required immediate surgery, diagnosed radiologically and/or histologically.
The trial excluded those who received prior systemic anticancer therapy and those with metastatic disease.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1 by IRC in VHL disease-associated RCC.

citations.quote: Primary: ORR per RECIST 1.1 in VHL disease-associated
The confirmed ORR (per RECIST 1.1 by IRC) for VHL disease-associated RCC tumors was 36.1% (95% CI=24.2% to 49.4%), with all responders having a PR [Table 5].
To support the proposed indication, a single-arm study (MK-6482-004; study 004) was conducted in 61 patients with VHL-associated RCC receiving 120 mg QD dose of belzutifan.

result.text: At the primary analysis cutoff, confirmed ORR per RECIST 1.1 by IRC was 36.1% (22/61; 95% CI 24.2, 49.4), all partial responses; median DoR not reached. At an updated cutoff ORR was 49.2% (95% CI 36.1, 62.3).

citations.quote: cutoff, the confirmed ORR (primary efficacy endpoint) per RECIST 1.1 was 36.1% (22 out of 61; 95% CI: 24.2%, 49.4%).
The IRC-assessed ORR with a median follow-up time of 22 months (range 4.2, 30.1) was 49.2% (36.1, 62.3) for VHL-RCC; all partial responses. Median DoR was not reached (range 2.8+ to 22.3+ months).

indication.text: WELIREG is indicated for treatment of adult patients with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease who require therapy for associated renal cell carcinoma (RCC), central nervous system (CNS) hemangioblastomas, or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET), not requiring immediate surgery.

target_moa.text: Belzutifan is a first-in-class oral small molecule hypoxia-inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF-2α) inhibitor that binds to HIF-2α, preventing its heterodimerization with ARNT (HIF-1β) and subsequent DNA binding, thereby decreasing transcription of HIF-2α target genes that promote tumor survival.

citations.quote: Belzutifan (Welireg, MK-6482, PT2977) is a first-in-class oral small molecule with an established pharmacological class of hypoxia-inducible factor inhibitor that binds to HIF-2\alpha.

Belzutifan binds to HIF-2\alpha and prevents its heterodimerization and its subsequent binding to DNA leading to decreased transcription and expression of HIF-2\alpha target genes that regulate hypoxia and promote tumor survival.
Belzutifan is a small molecule inhibitor of hypoxia inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF 2\alpha), which is overexpressed in many tumors.

key_safety.text: Most common (≥25%) adverse reactions including laboratory abnormalities were decreased hemoglobin, anemia, fatigue, increased creatinine, headache, dizziness, increased glucose, and nausea. In Study 004 anemia occurred in 90% of patients (7% Grade 3). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 15% of patients.

citations.quote: Most common (\ge 25\%) adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, were decreased hemoglobin, anemia, fatigue, increased creatinine, headache, dizziness, increased glucose, and nausea. (6.1)
In Study 004, anemia occurred in 90% of patients and 7% had Grade 3 anemia [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].
Serious adverse reactions occurred in 15% of patients who received WELIREG, including anemia, hypoxia, anaphylaxis reaction, retinal detachment, and central retinal vein occlusion (1 patient each).

detail.text: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Exposure to WELIREG during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm; verify pregnancy status prior to initiation; advise effective non-hormonal contraception as WELIREG can render some hormonal contraceptives ineffective.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

- Exposure to WELIREG during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm.
- Verify pregnancy status prior to the initiation of WELIREG.
- Advise patients of these risks and the need for effective non-hormonal contraception. WELIREG can render some hormonal contraceptives ineffective [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.3), *Drug Interactions* (7.2), *Use in Specific Populations* (8.1, 8.3)].
Risk and Risk Management	No REMS will be required.
